maya: Heads-up — hitting a weird ESM/CJS interop issue when running the Node SDK on Next edge (Vercel). Token auth ends up undefined in the edge build only. Anyone seen this?

sam: ugh, seen similar when package exports aren't set. are you shipping both .mjs and .cjs bundles? repo link?

maya: shipping dist/index.mjs (ESM) and dist/index.cjs. package.json has "type": "module" for the source build. Next edge fails at runtime with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getToken')`. local node (cjs) works fine.

darren: can you paste the import you use in the edge function? Next edge requires ESM style imports.

maya: yep: `const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood-sdk')` — i realize that's wrong for edge but some consumers still use it. In the edge bundle the require seems to pull the cjs stub which expects `module.exports.default` shape and gets confused.

nate: try updating package.json exports so bundlers pick the right entry. something like:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
That forces ESM consumers to get the mjs file.

maya: I tried that and Vite respected it, but Next edge still bundled an intermediate wrapper that changed the default shape.

jules: Next's internal bundler (turbo/webpack/next) sometimes rewrites imports for edge. Another approach is to provide a single ESM entry and ship a CJS compat file that `export default` correctly. e.g. dist/index.cjs: `module.exports = require('./index.mjs').default` — ugly but works.

sam: also check for top-level `exports.default` vs named exports. If your ESM bundle uses `export default RedwoodClient`, then `const { RedwoodClient } = await import('redwood-sdk')` won't work; you'd need `const { default: RedwoodClient } = await import(...)` or `const RedwoodClient = (await import(...)).default`.

maya: ok — current ESM build exports `export default RedwoodClient`. We assumed named export but apparently not. Changing to named export might break existing code.

darren: another runtime-safe pattern is to support both shapes in the entry. e.g. in dist/index.mjs:
```js
export function makeClient(opts) { return new RedwoodClient(opts) }
export default RedwoodClient
```
This gives both named and default consumers something to use.

maya: good idea. two follow-ups: 1) streaming responses — edge function needs `Response` with ReadableStream. Our streaming handler uses Node stream (stream.Readable). Next edge converts differently. Anyone using the SDK streaming in edge?

nate: streaming across edge often needs web stream API. If SDK exposes Node streams, we wrap: `Readable.toWeb(nodeStream)` or use `web-streams-polyfill` for older Node. On Vercel edge, prefer using the `new ReadableStream({ pull(controller) { ... }})` web API.

jules: we should document both patterns in dev docs: "Edge streaming (web streams)" vs "Node streaming (stream.Readable)". Also call out that `fetch` in edge returns a web stream body.

maya: thanks — last thing: auth setup. The token call path uses `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` in our lib which is undefined in edge because Next replaces process.* at build time or strips it. Folks should use `const token = await getTokenFromPlatform()` or pass token explicitly to client creation.

sam: yep, recommend passing explicit token to create client in edge code. Env vars in Next edge need special handling: `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` gets inlined, but server-only envs don't.

ci-bot: workflow/build #3456 — ran tests for branches/* — 12/12 checks passed :white_check_mark:

maya: pinging @darren and @jules for a quick CR on the export shape change. I can open a tiny PR to add named exports + adjust package.json exports.

darren: will review in ~1h. quick note: add a tiny unit test that imports via dynamic import and asserts default + named exist. avoids regressions.

jules: also add a one-liner to docs in devex/edge-streaming.md and call out `exports` mapping.

maya: sweet. I'll draft PR and link it here. thanks all :sparkles:
